title: 74-year-old GOP candidate’s ‘corny’ Kendrick Lamar-inspired AI video is horrifying people
source_used: The National News Desk (Scripps), via KATU and WJLA
key_facts: Sen. Marsha Blackburn, 74, Republican candidate for governor of Tennessee, posted a 12-second AI video of herself lip-syncing to Kendrick Lamar's 'Not Like Us' on X on Tuesday (13 Oct 2026).
Other Tennessee Republicans appear as backup dancers: Rep. Tim Burchett, Sen. Bill Hagerty, state Sen. Brent Taylor and Knox County Mayor Glenn Jacobs, who wears his WWE 'Kane' outfit.
The caption 'Tomorrow. Ready to roll' referred to early voting starting in Tennessee on Wednesday.
Democratic nominee Jerri Green replied that this is what she meant when she asked supporters to stop using AI for her campaign.
Former Rep. Adam Kinzinger wrote 'Boomer thinks AI makes her look cool.'
Blackburn told WZTV a county commissioner made the video and it is 'a funsie'.
quote_evidence: "Tomorrow. Ready to roll," 74-year-old Blackburn posted on X on Tuesday with a 12-second AI video of herself lip-syncing to Lamar's "Not Like Us".
"When I say please stop using AI to support our campaign, this is what I mean..." Green posted.
Blackburn told WZTV... "it's a funsie. Everybody get out and vote!"
why_it_matters_hint: Campaign use of AI video is drawing ridicule in a governor's race as early voting starts.
notes: AL.com original blocked (403); text from The National News Desk syndicated on KATU and WJLA, which relays Mediaite. Posted 13 Oct, coverage 14 Oct.
